title: Regression Testing Safety Across Model Updates: Detecting Silent Safety Regressions

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain: fine-tuning can silently remove safety properties; a regression suite detects this. Directly addresses a known attack vector (Qi et al. 2023). Provides a missing feedback loop between model updates and safety assurance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a pytest-style harness that runs a fixed prompt set against model checkpoints is standard software engineering. Using open-weight model checkpoints from HuggingFace is well-documented. Accessible to CS beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Building the suite, curating the prompt set with expected labels, and testing across multiple checkpoints or fine-tuning steps is moderate scope. The CI/CD framing adds infrastructure complexity. Achievable in 30 hours if limited to a small suite and 2-3 checkpoints.

novelty.reasoning: Qi et al. (ICLR 2024, arXiv:2310.03693) established that fine-tuning compromises safety with as few as 10 examples. Extensive 2024-2025 follow-ups document 20-80% refusal rate deterioration (SORRY-Bench, AdvBench, HEx-PHI). Multiple mitigation approaches exist: SaLoRA (ICLR 2025) preserves safety features during fine-tuning, Dynamic Safety Shaping (2025) uses fine-grained safety signals, and model merging approaches (arXiv:2412.19512). However, these focus on preventing degradation during fine-tuning rather than providing a pytest-style regression testing harness that continuously monitors safety across model checkpoints. The CI/CD integration angle — a reusable test suite that runs automatically against each checkpoint — is a software engineering contribution not directly published, though the underlying safety benchmarks it would use already exist.

SORRY-Bench.details: Confirmed as safety benchmark. Reports refusal rate deterioration metrics. Relevant as existing evaluation tool.
